name: Compute Hijacking
description:
Adversaries may leverage the compute resources of co-opted systems to complete resource-intensive tasks, which may impact system and/or hosted service availability. 

One common purpose for [Compute Hijacking](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/001) is to validate transactions of cryptocurrency networks and earn virtual currency. Adversaries may consume enough system resources to negatively impact and/or cause affected machines to become unresponsive.(Citation: Kaspersky Lazarus Under The Hood Blog 2017) Servers and cloud-based systems are common targets because of the high potential for available resources, but user endpoint systems may also be compromised and used for [Compute Hijacking](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/001) and cryptocurrency mining.(Citation: CloudSploit - Unused AWS Regions) Containerized environments may also be targeted due to the ease of deployment via exposed APIs and the potential for scaling mining activities by deploying or compromising multiple containers within an environment or cluster.(Citation: Unit 42 Hildegard Malware)(Citation: Trend Micro Exposed Docker APIs)

Additionally, some cryptocurrency mining malware identify then kill off processes for competing malware to ensure it’s not competing for resources.(Citation: Trend Micro War of Crypto Miners)

telemetry.name: Container Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a runtime container object.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect runtime create events and image/container IDs; correlate with API audit to establish the initiating identity.

providers.name: Docker Engine events
providers.scope: Daemon lifecycle events for containers and images; collect continuously.

providers.name: Kubernetes API audit
providers.scope: Control-plane context in Kubernetes, not a replacement for runtime observations.

configuration: Subscribe to the lab daemon event stream with filters for the relevant object/action; send it to a durable collector.
Record runtime/container ID, image digest, action, timestamp and host. Join orchestrator identities where available.
Use a protected collector connection. Docker socket access is privileged; never expose it publicly or grant it to the website.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Runtime event history is bounded and can be lost without continuous collection. Image tags are mutable; pin digests. A lifecycle event is not a full process or file audit.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per workload image and namespace: rare process starts, unexpected image/privilege changes and new network relationships. Use workload/deployment identity, not short-lived container IDs alone.

telemetry.name: Host Status
telemetry.description: Host health and availability observations such as heartbeat, shutdown or degraded state.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect agent heartbeat and OS health independently; record missed polls, last-seen time and monitor health.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

telemetry.name: Instance Start
telemetry.description: A request to start a stopped compute instance and its resulting state.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect start APIs and instance-state transitions with request IDs; distinguish accepted from completed.

providers.name: AWS CloudTrail
providers.scope: Management-plane API activity; supported resource/data events require separate selectors.

providers.name: Azure Monitor Activity Log
providers.scope: Azure resource control-plane operations; resource data-plane logs are separate.

providers.name: Google Cloud Audit Logs
providers.scope: Admin Activity and other categories; configure Data Access where required.

configuration: In the isolated account/project/subscription, route administrative audit logs to a protected destination with retention and access controls.
Select the relevant service, regions and read/write operations. Confirm whether the API below is a management or data event in the provider documentation.
Preserve actor/session, resource, request ID, service, operation, region and error details. Check delivery latency and avoid logging credentials or sensitive request bodies.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: AWS, Azure and Google expose different APIs and event schemas. An accepted API request does not prove the final resource state; join asynchronous outcomes and inventory.

sources.title: AWS EC2 API logging with CloudTrail

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per account, role, region and API: rare actions, new role-resource relationships, enumeration bursts and configuration changes. Separate deployment automation and organization-level administrative activity.

telemetry.name: Network Connection Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of an endpoint network connection linked to a process.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable scoped Sysmon NetworkConnect (3), disabled by default, or a platform-equivalent process-aware network sensor.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

telemetry.name: Network Traffic Content
telemetry.description: Packet or decoded application-protocol content visible at a network sensor.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope approved packet capture/protocol content collection to the lab flow; retain capture provenance and truncation indicators.

providers.name: Zeek
providers.scope: Connection and protocol metadata from traffic visible to the sensor.

providers.name: Suricata EVE
providers.scope: Configured flow, alert, DNS, HTTP, TLS and protocol records.

configuration: Use an authorized lab TAP/SPAN, virtual mirror or gateway interface. Define which traffic crosses it; avoid assuming visibility into every segment.
Enable the required Zeek analyzers or Suricata EVE event types. Export logs with sensor identity, clock synchronization and flow correlation identifiers.
Monitor capture loss, truncation and exporter sampling. Capture payload only with approval and restrictive retention; encryption normally prevents plaintext inspection.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Flows are not packet payloads. NAT, asymmetric routes, encryption, missing mirrors and sampling can hide attribution or content. A destination connection alone does not prove malicious intent.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per source and observation point: connection rate, destination-host/port fan-out, response/failure ratio and previously unseen destinations. Compare equivalent time windows; separate authorized scanners, NAT and sampling effects.

telemetry.name: Scheduled Job Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a scheduled execution object, including its trigger, principal and executable action.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit Other Object Access Events for Windows task creation (4698); retain task XML. For cron/systemd timers, collect scheduler definitions and change events separately.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

strategies.name: Multi-Platform Behavioral Detection for Compute Hijacking

analytics.name: Analytic 1489
analytics.guidance: Sustained execution of resource-intensive processes (e.g., cryptocurrency miners), often launched via scheduled tasks, WMI, or PowerShell. These processes frequently establish persistent external connections and attempt to evade detection using masqueraded or renamed binaries.

tuning.description: The executable name of the miner or wrapper—can vary across campaigns.
May differ depending on the mining pool or proxy server.
Useful for filtering known-good automation vs malicious task runners.

analytics.name: Analytic 1490
analytics.guidance: Unusual long-running processes consuming high CPU cycles (e.g., via 'top' or 'ps') initiated via cron, shell scripts, or Docker. Connections to known mining pools or DNS over HTTPS usage as evasion.

tuning.description: The miner's execution path and options may vary by campaign.
Environment-specific definition of anomalous CPU usage.

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Outbound connection to mining pool port (3333, 4444, 5555)

log_sources.name: linux:cron
log_sources.channel: Scheduled execution of unknown or unusual script/binary

analytics.name: Analytic 1491
analytics.guidance: Persistent or background daemons (e.g., plist or launchd jobs) spawning high-CPU processes like xmrig or cpuminer. Outbound encrypted traffic to IPs/domains commonly used by mining proxies.

tuning.description: May be disguised with benign-looking names.
Varying mining pool or obfuscated destination.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: launchd or cron spawning mining binaries

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Persistent outbound connections with consistent periodicity

analytics.name: Analytic 1492
analytics.guidance: Ephemeral or unauthorized container instantiation using public images (e.g., from DockerHub) that initiate high CPU usage shortly after startup. Often scheduled via Kubernetes or Docker socket abuse.

tuning.description: May vary depending on where the image is pulled from (registry or custom URL).

log_sources.name: NSM:Flow
log_sources.channel: Outbound traffic to mining pool upon container launch

analytics.name: Analytic 1493
analytics.guidance: Unauthorized instance creation in unmonitored or unused regions. Burst of compute-intensive jobs in spot instances or sudden spike in resource usage in legitimate VMs.

tuning.description: Adversaries may deploy resources in rarely used or misconfigured regions.
Used to evade detection with benign-looking tags or names.

log_sources.name: AWS:CloudWatch
log_sources.channel: Unusual CPU burst or metric anomalies
